what_matters.tag_note: Nvidia · results out · Tue 17 Nov after the close
what_matters.head: Nvidia's Q3 revenue was $115.8B, above the top of its own forecast range, and it forecast $130.0B for Q4.
what_matters.detail: Revenue rose 103% from a year earlier, against the company's forecast of $108.0B, plus or minus 2%. Analysts expected about $109.1B (LSEG, per CNBC). Adjusted earnings per share were $2.68; analysts expected $2.47 to $2.48. The Q4 forecast is $130.0B, plus or minus 3%, for a quarter with one extra week. Analysts expected $125.1B (LSEG, per CNBC; Investing.com gives $125.3B). The forecast gross margin is 71.0–72.0%, against 74.9% in Q3, and the forecast assumes no data-centre chip revenue from China. The shares closed down 0.4% before the results. On the call the board's chair said it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang and has hired a search firm to find a permanent chief executive (CNBC).

what_matters.head: The S&P 500 fund fell 1.01% on Tuesday, about 1.1 times its usual daily move. It was the index's fourth straight fall and its lowest close since 29 July (CNBC).
what_matters.detail: Software was hit hard: Salesforce lost 9.45% after OpenAI released new models, which revived worries that AI replaces software products (Motley Fool, Yahoo Finance). A run of technology outages at airlines, banks and other firms also weighed (Motley Fool). The chip fund was flat, up 0.17%, ahead of Nvidia's results. No watchlist name moved as much as 2 times its usual day.

what_matters.tag_note: Anthropic IPO · pricing expected tonight · trading Thu 19 Nov
what_matters.head: Anthropic's share sale is expected to price tonight, New York time, and to start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday.
what_matters.detail: The filing offers 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each. People who spoke to CNBC on Tuesday expect a price above that range (one report). Seven companies have agreed to buy $26.0B of non-voting stock at the IPO price once the sale completes. At the $74 midpoint that is $10.0B each for Nvidia and Google, $2.5B for AMD, $1.0B each for Broadcom, Micron and Microsoft, and $0.5B for TSMC (Anthropic's filing of 10 Nov). Fundstrat's Tom Lee wrote on Tuesday that the sale is drawing cash out of other positions (Yahoo Finance).

after_data.text: Nvidia rose about 4.8% in after-hours trading (Investing.com); CNBC's later update said nearly 4%. CoreWeave and Nebius jumped, and AMD and Broadcom gained modestly (Yahoo Finance). None of this is in Tuesday's US closing prices.
South Korea's KOSPI rose 1.4% and Japan's Nikkei 0.4%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 1.2% and Singapore's Straits Times Index 1.1% (Investing.com). Not in Tuesday's US prices.

House committee chairs said on Tuesday that Huang has agreed to appear for transcribed interviews. Nvidia set up a board committee on national security and export controls (AP). CNBC relayed a Wall Street Journal report that the SEC is investigating Nvidia (one report). The time of day of each is not known, so Tuesday's prices may or may not include them.

This answers yesterday's question. Tuesday's city-run mediation session ended without agreement. The union will put management's proposed framework to a member vote before a second session on 26 Nov at 16:30 (unverified: Liberty Times, as recorded in the catalyst notes).

out.text: Also in the filing: $28.1B returned to shareholders in the quarter. Supply commitments rose to $390B from $279B, mainly for multi-year memory supply. Customers took 64 days to pay, up from 60, partly on longer payment terms for some customers. The 10-Q is due in the coming weeks.

movers.why: GuruFocus put Tuesday's fall down to Monday's US chip rule. Besides the country licences, the rule tightens the checks that chip foundries and packagers must run on designers from restricted countries. TSMC was down 4.26% at 10:45 a.m. New York.

Hit its lowest since 24 Sep as its Ignite conference opened. One article cites doubts about the cost of its AI build-out, high interest rates and last week's Microsoft 365 outage (BeInCrypto via Yahoo Finance). Software shares fell broadly on the day.

DBS, OCBC and UOB each fell between 1.4% and 1.6% this morning. The Straits Times Index opened 1.2% lower as investors stayed cautious about AI shares despite Nvidia's forecast (MT Newswires). No report specific to the banks was found.
Up so far today as Asian chip shares went different ways after Nvidia's results; South Korea's KOSPI rose 1.4% (Investing.com). No SK Hynix news was found.
